bugs.error_message: Uncaught TypeError: s.points.show is not a function (at uplot.js drawSeries)
bugs.root_cause: uPlot wraps series.points.show into a callable via fnOrSelf when the series is created. A later effect ([renderDataPoints, pointRadius]) reassigned s.points.show = renderDataPoints && (s.points.show ?? false); when renderDataPoints was false, the && short-circuited to the literal boolean false, overwriting the function. The next redraw called s.points.show(...) and crashed since it was no longer callable.
bugs.fix: Compute the desired show boolean separately (shouldShowPoints = renderDataPoints && s.show !== false) and always assign a function: s.points.show = () => shouldShowPoints.

bugs.error_message: Line Confidence chart shows "No data available" after navigating between sensors, even though the sensor has measurements (verified via direct API call)
bugs.root_cause: LineConfidenceProvider was rendered without a key, so React Router reuses the same component instance when navigating from one sensor to another instead of unmounting/remounting it. All useState in LineConfidenceContext.tsx (selectedTimeRange, minFilterValueInput, maxFilterValueInput, additionalSensorInfos/Data) survives the navigation; the existing reset effect only cleared aggregationInterval/aggregationValue/hasUserSelectedAggregation. A stale time-range or value filter from the previously viewed sensor gets applied to the new sensor, filtering every aggregation bucket down to zero and eventually landing on the No data available state after the interval auto-widen effect exhausts second->minute->hour->day->week->month.
bugs.fix: Added key={campaignId-stationId-sensorId} to LineConfidenceProvider in LineConfidenceViz.tsx so switching sensors forces a full remount, resetting all context state instead of relying on an incomplete manual reset effect.

bugs.error_message: Line Confidence chart continuously flashes loading/chart and never settles or displays data
bugs.root_cause: The uPlot setScale hook unconditionally called onViewDomainChange (LineConfidenceChart setViewDomain) and onBrush (Chart.tsx setSelectedTimeRange) on every scale change, including ones triggered programmatically by our own mount/update effects (u.setScale for x/y). Setting selectedTimeRange re-queries useListConfidenceValues with new start/end dates, producing new aggregatedData/minValue/maxValue, which re-runs the update-data effect and calls u.setScale again, refiring the hook and looping indefinitely (setSelectedTimeRange -> refetch -> setScale -> setSelectedTimeRange...). uPlot also defers its internal commit() (which fires the setScale hook) to a microtask, so a naive ref flag set/reset synchronously around the setScale calls did not actually bracket the hook firing.
bugs.fix: Added an isProgrammaticScaleUpdate ref that the setScale hook checks and bails out on. Wrapped the effects own setData/setScale calls in u.batch(), which uPlot documents as committing synchronously (skipping the microtask queue) specifically so the ref flag correctly brackets the hook firing.

bugs.error_message: Line Confidence chart never settles: repeated GET .../measurements/confidence-intervals requests with end_date walking backward by exactly 1 hour each time, chart never displays
bugs.root_cause: Reproduced headlessly with Playwright (console + network capture) and confirmed via added mount/unmount logging that UPlotChart was genuinely unmounting and remounting every cycle (not just re-rendering) with dataArray shrinking each time. Chart.tsx gates the entire chart subtree on `{aggregatedData && (...)}`; TanStack Query v5 resets `data` to undefined while a query with a changed queryKey is in flight (no placeholderData configured), so every time selectedTimeRange changed, aggregatedData went null and unmounted UPlotChart. Each fresh uPlot instance performs its own internal initial auto-range from the data on construction, firing the setScale hook before isProgrammaticScaleUpdate (the bug-096 fix) is even relevant, since it is a brand-new ref on a brand-new instance. That phantom auto-range was treated as a user brush, calling onBrush -> setSelectedTimeRange with a slightly narrower window, triggering another refetch, another unmount/remount, converging by roughly one hour narrower each cycle, forever.
bugs.fix: 1) In UPlotChart.tsx setScale hook, added `if (u.cursor.event == null) return;` alongside the existing isProgrammaticScaleUpdate guard — cursor.event is only ever set by a real DOM mouse event, so this ignores uPlot-internal auto-ranging (construction-time or data-driven) and only treats genuine drag/zoom interactions as a user brush. 2) Added `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` (TanStack Query v5) to useListConfidenceValues.ts and useList.ts so data stays populated during a start/end-date refetch instead of resetting to undefined, preventing the Chart.tsx `{aggregatedData && ...}` gate from unmounting UPlotChart on every refetch in the first place. Verified fixed via headless Playwright reproduction: request count dropped from an unbounded loop to exactly 2 (one per data source), and the chart rendered real data.

bugs.error_message: Line Confidence uPlot chart shows no axis tick numbers or axis titles, and gridlines render purple instead of gray
bugs.root_cause: Two separate bugs. (1) axes[].values callbacks generated their own 5 evenly-spaced tick positions via a local generateTicks() helper instead of formatting uPlot own computed tick positions (the splits argument), so the returned label array did not correspond to the gridlines uPlot actually drew and rendering silently produced nothing. (2) axes[].grid.stroke / ticks.stroke / stroke were set to var(--gray-300) / var(--gray-600), which are also not defined anywhere as real CSS custom properties, and even if they were, uPlot draws on <canvas> which cannot resolve CSS var() the way SVG/DOM styles can -- ctx.strokeStyle silently ignores an unresolvable value and keeps whatever color was set by the previous draw call (the series line), producing purple gridlines.
bugs.fix: Rewrote axes[].values as (u, splits) => splits.map(v => formatter(v)), using uPlot own tick positions. Replaced the var(--gray-XXX) references with literal hex matching tailwind.config.ts secondary gray scale (300/600). Added axes[0].space to prevent tick label overlap, and repurposed the previously-dead xFormatterOverview prop as a short date-only axis-tick formatter (formatDateInZone) distinct from the full date+time xFormatter used for the crosshair tooltip.

bugs.error_message: Line Confidence chart shows data only in a small sliver near the right edge of the plot; the rest of the (much wider) date range is completely blank, despite the API returning a full, evenly-distributed dataset across the whole range
bugs.root_cause: Two compounding bugs. (1) getGapThresholdMs ignored the caller-supplied gapThresholdMinutes prop entirely (parameter was literally named _gapThresholdMinutes) and used a hardcoded per-aggregation-interval table copied from the old pre-uPlot D3 implementation (5 minutes for 'minute' aggregation). Any sensor whose real reporting cadence is coarser than that hardcoded value (e.g. hourly telemetry, 3600s apart, aggregated at the 'minute' level) had EVERY single consecutive pair of points flagged as a gap. (2) processSensorData's gap handling pushed `null` directly into the x-axis timestamp array (xs.push(null)) as a separator. uPlot's AlignedData type requires the x-array to contain only real numbers -- only the y-series arrays may contain null. With nulls scattered through data[0], uPlot's internal auto-range min/max computation (which coerces null to 0 in numeric comparisons) computed an x-min near epoch 0 instead of the true data start, so the real April-September 2026 data compressed into a thin sliver at the far right of a scale effectively spanning from 1970. Confirmed by direct network-response inspection (full, evenly-distributed 3590 buckets across 6 months) versus a debug dump of the transformed xs array immediately before passing it to `new uPlot()`, and by re-reading uPlot AlignedData's TypeScript type (xValues: number[] | TypedArray, no null variant, vs y-values which explicitly allow null).
bugs.fix: getGapThresholdMs now simply converts the passed gapThresholdMinutes to ms and no longer reads a hardcoded per-interval table. processSensorData no longer pushes null into xs; a detected gap now pushes a real, monotonic timestamp (lastTs + 1) with null y-values instead. Also discovered spanGaps was set to true on every series, which per uPlot's own docs means 'null data values will not cause line breaks' -- the OPPOSITE of the code's own stated intent ('Inserts null at gap boundaries so uPlot's spanGaps breaks lines'). Changed spanGaps to false everywhere so a real gap (now correctly threshold-calibrated) actually renders as a visible break instead of being silently bridged over.

bugs.error_message: Chart hover legend/crosshair readout: 'Time' value never displays (always blank/wrong); labels read 'Primary'/'Primary Upper'/'Primary Lower' which are unclear to users
bugs.root_cause: uPlot's Series.value callback signature is (self, rawValue, seriesIdx, idx) -- the second argument is already the resolved raw value for that series at the cursor position, not an index. The Time series' callback was `(u, i) => u.data[0][i]`, treating the raw millisecond timestamp (a huge number) as an array index into u.data[0], indexing far out of bounds and always returning undefined.
bugs.fix: Rewrote the Time series' value callback to use the already-resolved rawValue directly, formatted through a new full date+time formatter (legendTimeFormatter, wraps xFormatter). Renamed legend labels: 'Primary' -> 'Value', 'Primary Upper'/'Primary Lower' -> 'Upper Bound'/'Lower Bound', 'Sensor N' -> 'Sensor N Value'/'Sensor N Upper Bound'/'Sensor N Lower Bound' for comparison sensors.

bugs.error_message: "Compare" feature: selecting a sensor and clicking "Add Selected Sensors" adds it to the "Comparison Sensors" list, but no second line or legend row ever appears on the chart
bugs.root_cause: uPlot's series list (opts.series, and therefore the number/identity of series the live instance knows about) is fixed at construction time (new uPlot(opts, data, target)). The 'Initialize uPlot' effect ran only once on mount ([] deps); the separate 'Update data' effect only called u.setData()/u.setScale() when props changed, never u.addSeries(). When a comparison sensor was added after mount, buildSeriesConfig recomputed a series array with 3 more entries and dataArray grew 3 more columns, but the already-constructed uPlot instance was never told about the new series -- setData() with more data columns than configured series silently does not add a new line or legend row.
bugs.fix: Changed the mount effect's dependency array from [] to [series.length, secondaryUnitLabel], and removed the isInitialized early-return guard, so the effect properly destroys and recreates the whole uPlot instance whenever the series count changes (comparison sensor added/removed) or a secondary axis needs to appear/disappear. This also naturally re-reads all other current prop values (colors, formatters, renderDataPoints) fresh at recreation time. bugs.error_message: Chart legend (Time/Value/Upper Bound/... row below the chart) overflows past its container into the page footer, worse with more comparison sensors added
bugs.root_cause: The outer container div that uPlot mounts into had a hardcoded CSS height (style={{height: dimensions.height}}), the same value passed to uPlot as the canvas height. uPlot renders its legend table as a DOM sibling below the canvas, inside that same container -- so the true content height is canvas height + legend height, which grows with each comparison sensor's legend row. Since the container's fixed height only accounted for the canvas, the legend simply overflowed (default overflow: visible) past the bottom of the box into whatever rendered next on the page (the site footer).
bugs.fix: Removed the fixed height from the container div in the main render path so it sizes to its actual content (canvas + legend) instead of being capped at canvas-only height. Also changed the ResizeObserver to only track width, not height -- height was previously fed back from the observed container size, which would have created a feedback loop (legend grows -> observed container height grows -> re-applied as canvas height -> grows again) once the container's own height was no longer pinned.

bugs.error_message: Clicking publish in the Upstream UI fails when the CKAN dataset was already created during ingestion.
bugs.root_cause: The UI omitted patch_existing_ckan_dataset, so the backend rejected the existing deterministic CKAN dataset as a name conflict instead of updating its visibility.
bugs.fix: UI station and campaign publish requests now set patchExistingCkanDataset=true, allowing the existing CKAN dataset to be patched public during publication.
